headline: Market closed for weekend; focus on upcoming week's IPO rush, FPI outflows, and global crude trends.

marketStatus.message: Market is closed today because it is a weekend. It will reopen on Monday, 21 September.

why: Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) withdrew ₹20,974 crore from Indian equities in September due to global uncertainty.
Crude oil price movements and the West Asia situation continue to drive broader market sentiment.
FMCG companies are likely to hold prices steady through the festive season despite underlying cost pressures.
Investors are closely tracking upcoming corporate actions across multiple stocks in the week ahead.
whatHappening: A major primary market surge is expected with 19 IPO issues opening to raise ₹4,169 crore.
NMDC chairman announced the company is targeting 60 million tonnes (MT) of iron ore production this fiscal year.
Sensex and Nifty trailed fixed deposit returns in a 3-year bull market comparison test.
Grey Market Premium (GMP) for NSE unlisted shares dropped to its lowest level since its IPO announcement.
summary: Indian stock markets are closed today for the weekend and will reopen on Monday, September 21. Key triggers for the coming week include persistent FPI sell-offs exceeding ₹20,000 crore alongside global crude oil volatility. Primary market activity will be in high focus with 19 IPO issues launching to raise over ₹4,100 crore.
